messages.content: I have the Palm Springs flights narrowed down. Now compare the three resort quotes for November 14-18 as complete stays, not by the headline nightly rate. We also want two treatments Saturday afternoon.

Send me the three quotes, including room type, taxes and fees, deposit and cancellation language, and any spa information you have. I’ll normalize each to four nights for two adults and separate included value from charges we would incur anyway.

Desert Palms shows a garden king at $389 a night. The checkout page adds a $55 nightly resort fee, $32 nightly parking, and taxes. Its displayed total is $2,214.40. Cancellation is allowed until 4:00 p.m. seven days before arrival, and it takes a one-night deposit.

Does the $2,214.40 total already include all four parking charges, and will you actually have a car? Also, is the deposit calculated from the base room rate or the first night including tax and the resort fee?
The total includes parking. We plan to use rideshares, so remove it if the charge is avoidable. The deposit line says $506.18, including tax and the first resort fee.

Then Desert Palms should be $2,086.40 if parking is charged only when a vehicle is parked: $2,214.40 less four $32 charges. I would still obtain written confirmation that parking is usage-based, because some booking summaries display it even when it is not part of the amount due. The deposit is $506.18, and the cancellation cutoff is Friday, November 7 at 4:00 p.m. local hotel time, assuming the wording is exactly seven days before the November 14 arrival.

Second is Arroyo House. A courtyard king is $465 nightly. The four-night total is $2,332.80, including taxes and all mandatory fees. It includes daily breakfast for two and a $150 spa credit, but they charge a two-night deposit of $1,166.40. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. ten days before arrival.

That puts Arroyo House $246.40 above Desert Palms after removing avoidable parking. Its included $150 spa credit reduces the effective difference to $96.40 if you use the full credit. Breakfast can close the remainder, but I’ll keep it as a benefit rather than subtracting an assumed meal value. The tradeoff is cash flow and an earlier cutoff: a $1,166.40 deposit and cancellation by Tuesday, November 4 at 6:00 p.m. local time.

The third is Mesa Verde Retreat. The standard king sold out, so only a terrace studio remains. It is $539 a night and $2,548.16 total with taxes and fees. One-night deposit of $637.04. Cancellation is allowed until 3:00 p.m. three days before arrival. No breakfast or spa credit.

Mesa Verde is $461.76 above the adjusted Desert Palms total and $215.36 above Arroyo House. Its material advantage is flexibility: cancellation until Tuesday, November 11 at 3:00 p.m., with only $637.04 paid up front. The remaining terrace studio may also be a better room, but that is inventory-driven rather than a like-for-like value advantage.

I called the spas. Desert Palms can do a 50-minute massage at 1:00 and a facial at 3:30, but not together. Arroyo House has two 80-minute massages at 2:00. Mesa Verde has a massage and facial both at 2:30. Prices before gratuity are $185 each at Desert Palms, $245 each at Arroyo House, and $220 each at Mesa Verde. Apply the credit correctly.

Including the two treatments, before gratuity, the trip totals are: Desert Palms $2,456.40; Arroyo House $2,672.80 after applying the $150 credit to the $490 treatment charge; and Mesa Verde $2,988.16. Arroyo House is therefore $216.40 above Desert Palms on lodging plus spa, while Mesa Verde is $531.76 above it. Breakfast remains an additional Arroyo House benefit. Arroyo and Mesa Verde both provide simultaneous appointments; Desert Palms separates you by two and a half hours and uses shorter treatments.
Check that Arroyo calculation. The spa said the credit cannot be used for gratuity, but it can be split between both treatments.

The calculation already treats the credit that way: two massages total $490, the $150 credit reduces the treatment balance to $340, and $2,332.80 plus $340 equals $2,672.80 before gratuity. Splitting the credit between treatments does not change the combined amount. Gratuity would be paid separately and should generally be based on the undiscounted treatment prices unless the spa states otherwise.
What are the true amounts due now and later for each hotel? Assume no parking at Desert Palms, but flag anything that still needs confirmation.

Desert Palms: $506.18 due as the deposit and $1,580.22 remaining on the adjusted $2,086.40 lodging total. Confirm that the hotel will remove all $128 of parking and that the displayed balance updates accordingly. Arroyo House: $1,166.40 due now and $1,166.40 remaining on lodging; the $340 net spa charge is separate unless prepaid. Mesa Verde: $637.04 due now and $1,911.12 remaining on lodging, with $440 in treatments separate. Those later figures exclude gratuities and incidental holds.
The Arroyo booking page also says the benefit package is valid only on the courtyard king rate and the spa credit is once per stay, not daily. That is the room I’m viewing.

Then the Arroyo benefits align with the quoted room: daily breakfast for two across the four mornings and one $150 spa credit for the entire stay. The comparison uses one credit, so no adjustment is needed. Capture the package name and benefit wording in the confirmation because a generic room-only confirmation could omit them.
Are any of these cancellation terms meaningfully better once the spa appointments are considered? The spas have separate policies.

Yes, but I need the treatment cancellation deadlines to assess the complete exposure. The room windows alone favor Mesa Verde, followed by Desert Palms, then Arroyo House. A flexible room does not help much if $440 of spa services becomes nonrefundable earlier.

Desert Palms requires 24 hours for spa cancellations. Arroyo requires 48 hours and a card guarantee but no prepayment. Mesa Verde requires 72 hours and charges 50% when booked, refundable until that deadline.

Mesa Verde still has the broadest room cancellation window, but its spa creates the largest early cash commitment: $220 charged when the treatments are reserved, refundable through Wednesday, November 12 at 2:30 p.m. Arroyo’s spa has no advance charge and can be canceled through Thursday, November 13 at 2:00 p.m.; its room, however, locks first on November 4. Desert Palms has the latest spa deadline, Friday, November 14 at the applicable appointment time, but its room locks on November 7. All deadlines should be confirmed in Palm Springs local time and checked for wording such as ‘24 hours prior’ versus ‘by the previous day.’
Rank the three complete options. Give more weight to having the treatments together and to included value, but do not ignore the deposit or cancellation risk.

1. Arroyo House. It has the strongest complete experience: simultaneous 80-minute treatments, $150 applied to them, and breakfast for two each morning. Its $2,672.80 lodging-and-treatment total is only $216.40 above Desert Palms before assigning any value to breakfast. The drawbacks are the $1,166.40 deposit and the earliest room cancellation deadline.

2. Desert Palms. It is the cost leader at $2,456.40 including treatments, assuming parking is removed, and has a modest $506.18 deposit. It ranks second because the 50-minute services are not simultaneous and leave one person waiting between appointments. Its total is also not fully reliable until the no-parking adjustment is confirmed.

3. Mesa Verde Retreat. It offers simultaneous treatments and the best room flexibility, but the $2,988.16 combined total is substantially higher, breakfast is not included, and the spa takes $220 up front. The terrace studio and later room cutoff do not offset the $315.36 premium over Arroyo for this trip.
So what exactly should I hold, and what must be verified before I give either property a card? Nothing should be booked yet.

First choice: ask Arroyo House to place a courtesy hold, if available, on one courtyard king for November 14-18 and two 80-minute massages at 2:00 p.m. Saturday, November 15. Before providing a card, verify the $2,332.80 lodging total includes every mandatory fee and tax; the $1,166.40 deposit amount and refund method; the exact November 4 cancellation cutoff and local time; daily breakfast for two; one $150 spa credit that can be split across both treatments; and that both 2:00 p.m. appointments are held with no spa prepayment. Also confirm the credit applies to the quoted $490 treatment total and obtain the room and spa policies in writing.

Keep Desert Palms as the backup. Ask it to hold the garden king plus the 1:00 p.m. massage and 3:30 p.m. facial only if the holds are nonbinding. Require a revised lodging total of $2,086.40 with no parking charge, then verify the $506.18 deposit, November 7 room deadline, and 24-hour spa policy. Do not hold Mesa Verde unless flexibility becomes more important than cost. Nothing has been booked.
